### B119-F-CKSUM-IP: The IPv4 header checksum of the TCP fast path equals the Internet checksum, for all inputs

- Kind: functional. State: verified; the Lean proof is of a transcription of the RTL, not of the RTL itself; rests on a delegated acceptance of the Lean statement, not a human approval.
- Agreement: draft: no agreement recorded.
- Method mix required by its kind: not yet measured (brief 143a). Mutation score of its bench: not yet measured (brief 143b).
- Text: Brief 119's tcp_fast.sv builds the IPv4 header checksum from a precomputed template plus the changing fields. For all TTL, address and identification values it equals the complement of the ones' complement sum of the header, and the filled-in header sums to 0xFFFF.

### B119-F-CKSUM-TCP: The TCP checksum of the TCP fast path equals the Internet checksum, for all inputs and payloads up to 30 words

- Kind: functional. State: verified; the Lean proof is of a transcription of the RTL, not of the RTL itself; rests on a delegated acceptance of the Lean statement, not a human approval.
- Agreement: draft: no agreement recorded.
- Method mix required by its kind: not yet measured (brief 143a). Mutation score of its bench: not yet measured (brief 143b).
- Text: For all addresses, ports, sequence and acknowledgement numbers, windows and payloads of up to 30 sixteen-bit words, the checksum the RTL equations produce equals the complement of the ones' complement sum over pseudo-header, header and payload. The byte-pair swapping, the streaming receive check and the timing are not modelled.

### B119-F-CKSUM-MODEL: The ones' complement arithmetic the checksum equations rest on is correct, for lists of any length

- Kind: functional. State: verified; the Lean proof is of a transcription of the RTL, not of the RTL itself; rests on a delegated acceptance of the Lean statement, not a human approval.
- Agreement: draft: no agreement recorded.
- Method mix required by its kind: not yet measured (brief 143a). Mutation score of its bench: not yet measured (brief 143b).
- Text: The ones' complement sum of any list of 16-bit words equals the natural-number sum reduced mod 65535, and RFC 1624 equation 3 (incremental update) is correct for a header of any length when the new header is not all zero words; for an all-zero header it gives 0x0000. No current RTL patches a checksum in place; this is the arithmetic the fast path's template-plus-fields form relies on.

## Limits

- Verified never means interoperability with a device the design talks to unless a board measurement against that device is listed above; a design that checks its own output against its own model accepts its own symmetric mistakes.
- Verified never means timing beyond the stated corner: a post-route timing result is for the part, speed grade, clock and tool version in its evidence file, not for other corners, temperatures or devices.
- Verified never means beyond the widths and depths checked: a simulation covers the vectors it ran, a bounded formal result covers the stated depth only, and a per-width proof covers the widths it names; only a Lean proof marked all widths covers every width, and only for its model.
- Verified never means the requirement is the right one: the text of a requirement is the human's check (or the planner's, where the record says delegated), and a record shows that checks exist and pass, not that nothing was left out.
- Verified never means a hardware or board result unless a board measurement item is listed; a simulation is not the board.
- Verified is about the files in the manifest at the hashes given. A change to any of them makes the record out of date (the CI check fails), and the evidence stale until it is re-recorded.
- An agreement or acceptance recorded as delegated is the planner's decision on the owner's delegation, not a human sign-off; the record counts it apart.
- 2 requirements depend on an element outside the design and have not been closed by hardware, so they hold in simulation only: B119-F-MACPAIR, B119-F-REALPEER.
- 7 performance requirements are verified in simulation only, not measured on the board: B119-P-FIRSTBYTE, B119-P-IPCKSUM, B119-P-TCPCKSUM, B119-P-SEGMENT, B119-P-RATE, B119-P-TOP-SPEC, B119-P-TOP-VERDICT.
- 3 performance requirements are verified by post-route timing at one corner: B119-P-TIMING, B119-P-HOLD, B119-P-AREA.
- Lean proofs here are of a transcription of the RTL, not of the RTL itself: B119-F-CKSUM-IP, B119-F-CKSUM-TCP, B119-F-CKSUM-MODEL.

## Reproduce

Simulation and formal evidence only; this record never lists a board, programming or deploy command.

- the whole bench (cocotb on Icarus), the Python-side tests and the lint: `python3 -m pytest -q designs/b119_tcp_fast/tests/test_b119_model.py designs/b119_tcp_fast/tests/test_b119_rtl.py designs/b119_tcp_fast/tests/test_b119_lint.py`
- the same with the measurement records written (latency in clocks, outcomes, end-to-end figures): `B119_RECORD=$PWD/results/b119 python3 -m pytest -q designs/b119_tcp_fast/tests/test_b119_rtl.py`
- the seeded faults (every mutant of verif/mutants.yaml against the bench): `python3 designs/b119_tcp_fast/tests/run_mutants.py --jobs 2 --json results/b119/mutation.json`
